event.summary: Old-page stream fallback can reinterpret a literal paste as grid input
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Original consequence preserved: a page left open across the helm upgrade can draw grid messages as raw terminal output and lose its attachment on typing until reloaded. Revision from supplied g196/l1 and direct protocol source checks: some raw text is valid GridInput JSON, so malformed-input detachment is not the only input outcome. A literal small one-line JSON document shaped as Text can be decoded and its data string written to the program; JSON escapes become real control bytes, including Enter, without paste bracketing. This can turn a literal-document paste into command input and could lose user work. Suggested bucket: highest/security or loss of work for this wider input-authority consequence; the earlier no-established-highest assessment was limited to misdrawing and ordinary malformed input and must not suppress this route. Could-be-highest: yes. Source: parent terminal.js:2220-2235 sanitizes literal ESC only; :2650-2675 dispatches text pastes through insert; :4628-4634 calls term.paste; :4651-4666 chooses xterm for unknown kind. Parent term-bytes.js:55-56 does not unescape backslash sequences. The parent vendored xterm.js paste helper prepares text, brackets it only when decPrivateModes.bracketedPasteMode is true, and calls triggerDataEvent once; its default mode object sets bracketedPasteMode false. Parent terminal.js:4157-4159 encodes each sendData call into one binary WebSocket message, with :4191-4196 forwarding onData. New helm terminal.rs:762-773 forwards each binary message unchanged. At the reviewed revision GridInput is serde(tag=t) (grid.rs:1565-1566); Text carries a String (:1610-1612), decode uses serde_json::from_slice (:1650-1655), check_object merely checks the initial object delimiter (:558-565), and Text validation only bounds byte length (:1686-1693), with no ban on decoded control characters. HostAttach::send_input decodes before InputEncoder (grid_stream.rs:1064-1076); InputEncoder::encode Text is data.as_bytes(), distinct from the Paste branch and independent of the real program's bracketed-paste mode (grid_input.rs:175-176). Thus JSON escape interpretation and bypass of paste wrapping are confirmed source properties, not speculation that all old raw input must fail decode. Confidence: confirmed wire/encoder transformation conditional on the shipped legacy surface sending that complete paste; full end-to-end stale-page interlocks remain the interface owner g196's concern, whose latest supplied record establishes deliberate reconnect availability and no terminal build fence. No runtime behavior observed and no payload generated. Exact proposed_drop basis preserved for independent judgment: SPEC_impl.md, Grid streams, says ‘A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working.’ and ‘Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy.’ It describes grid misdrawing and malformed-input detachment, not specifically successful reinterpretation of a literal document. Do not accept or reject its scope here; no drop or lowering accepted. possible_cover: supplied g196/l1 is the originating same input-reinterpretation concern, with g082/c2 and g083/c5 corroboration; retain for consolidation, not a new independent discovery. Caveats: requires old page plus fresh unknown-kind xterm surface and valid small JSON paste; ordinary keystrokes generally detach. If that surface has already enabled bracketed paste from received bytes, the added wrapper prevents this exact complete-JSON route. A retained host/grid surface instead raises a stream error as recorded earlier. This acceptance cannot justify incompatible terminal-host wire behavior, which c2 separately refutes. This revises the original c1 rather than erasing its display/detach consequences or its proposed-drop basis.

event.summary: Old terminal contents and running jobs are deliberately retired
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e (and preceding documentation change dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4). TLDR: updating ends any remaining old terminals, their live agents and tabs, and their retained screens; the protocol no longer offers the old byte stream or terminal-kind reporting. Source: lib.rs removal of StreamKind, TerminalKind, SessionInfo terminal-kind fields, TabInfo::kind, Attach::grid and Attached::stream. Contract: SPEC.md:3003-3017, Terminal experience, explicitly requires retirement. Suggested bucket: highest/loss of processes and terminal contents. Confidence: confirmed contract and patch implications; not observed during execution. proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance, exact text: ‘This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.’ It further states: ‘one whose agent had already ended keeps its outcome, but its terminal’s last screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed.’ And: ‘A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.’ possible_cover: exact specification acceptance only; excluded coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: yes, established deliberate process and terminal-content loss; independent drop check required. Caveat: this group assesses removal and replacement contracts, not the separate startup retirement implementation. This is a proposed drop for independently checking an accepted consequence, not a claim that the retirement contradicts the spec.
